sources.entry: Beginning Game Programming with C++ and SDL

summary.title: Beginning Game Programming v2.0 (Lazy Foo' Productions)
summary.one_liner: A long, chapter-by-chapter C++ and SDL2 course that takes you from a first window to graphics, input, audio, timing, collision, threading, OpenGL and mobile ports.
takeaways: Covers the SDL2 basics: creating a window, loading and drawing images, and handling events and keyboard, mouse and gamepad input.
Explains hardware-accelerated rendering with textures, geometry, viewports, color keying, sprite sheets, alpha blending and rotation.
Teaches game-loop fundamentals: timing, frame rate calculation and capping, frame-independent movement, and collision detection.
Includes advanced topics such as threading primitives, render-to-texture, tiling, particle effects, and OpenGL integration.
Ends with porting to Android and iOS, including touch and multi-touch input.
summary.summary: This is an index page for a free tutorial series on game programming with C++ and SDL2, last updated July 28, 2025. The author says it is aimed at C++ programmers moving from text games to real-time graphical games. The page lists about 60 chapters in table-of-contents form, each with a one-line description. The page itself contains no code; the detailed material is in the individual chapter pages. The author also notes that SDL3 versions are in preparation and that some documentation links are broken due to SDL site redirects.
